Inputs:
  train_series    : DataFrame of ONE turbine's training rows (columns=feature_cols).

import numpy as np


def forecast(train_series, history_windows, feature_cols, target_col, input_len, output_len):
    w_idx = feature_cols.index("Wspd")
    p_idx = feature_cols.index(target_col)
    # Simple power curve: map binned wind speed to mean power
    bins = np.linspace(0, 25, 26)
    bin_indices = np.digitize(train_series["Wspd"], bins)
    curve = train_series.groupby(bin_indices)[target_col].mean()
    # Predict based on the last wind speed, adjusted by recent power bias
    last_w = history_windows[:, -1, w_idx]
    last_bin = np.digitize(last_w, bins)
    base = np.array([curve.get(b, curve.mean()) for b in last_bin])
    
    # Calculate recent bias (last 10 steps) to anchor the prediction
    recent_bias = np.mean(history_windows[:, -10:, p_idx], axis=1) - \
                  np.mean([curve.get(b, curve.mean()) for b in np.digitize(history_windows[:, -10:, w_idx].flatten(), bins)].reshape(-1, 10), axis=1)
    
    preds = base + 0.5 * recent_bias
    return np.clip(np.repeat(preds[:, None], output_len, axis=1), 0.0, None)
